title: PDE-Refiner: Achieving Accurate Long Rollouts with Neural PDE Solvers
layout_note: an unframed initial-prediction stage on the left, then one grey framed refinement step whose output returns to its input by a dashed loop running under the frame
grouping: Two stages under bold headings: 'Initial Prediction' (unframed) and 'Refinement process' (a light-grey rounded panel). The loop back from the refined output to the step's input runs outside the panel, along its bottom edge, labelled 'Repeat for k = 1, ..., K'.
shapes_depth: Flat; the network is a tall narrow rounded box with a light-green fill and vertical 'Neural Operator' text, drawn identically in both stages; data are small waveforms (blue for the previous state, orange for predictions, green for the predicted noise); circle glyphs for add and subtract.
proposed_highlight: No colour marks the contribution; the refinement step is the larger, grey-framed region, and its loop is the only dashed path in the figure.
lesson: Draw one iteration of a refinement loop as a framed step with every intermediate shown as data (noised input, predicted noise, refined output), and close the loop with one labelled dashed line outside the frame.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF first-page footer (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, NeurIPS 2023). Domain given as scientific-ml in the candidate list; the knowledge base's id for that area is ai4science.

arrangement.units: left: unframed 'Initial Prediction' stage; right: grey rounded 'Refinement process' panel holding one refinement step; a dashed loop under the panel returns the output to the input
arrangement.inputs_as: a blue waveform u(t - dt) and a flat line for the zero initial guess; the step index k enters each network from the top
arrangement.shared: the same light-green vertical Neural Operator box is drawn once per stage, fed by the same blue previous-state waveform

taxonomy.task: autoregressive neural PDE rollout with an iterative denoising refinement of each step
taxonomy.note: modality time-series stands for a 1-D PDE state evolving in time (the KS equation in this paper)

insights.structure: Two stages left to right, the second framed as one step that loops back on itself.
insights.data: Every state is a small waveform: the conditioning state in blue, the prediction (clean and noised) in orange, the predicted noise as a green noisy trace.
insights.emphasis: The refinement step gets the grey frame and most of the width; nothing else is highlighted.
insights.flow: Left to right on one baseline; the noise enters the add node from below, a curved line carries the noised input past the network to the subtract node, and a dashed path returns under the frame.
insights.avoid: The loop-back is a long dashed detour around the whole panel, and green fills the network box while also colouring the predicted-noise curve.

core.what: one refinement step framed in a grey panel (add noise, predict noise, subtract) with a dashed 'Repeat for k = 1..K' loop from its output back to its input

relations.form: the step is drawn once and closed by a dashed line from the refined output down and under the panel back to the step's input, labelled with the repeat range
'Initial Prediction' and 'Refinement process' side by side left to right, the network the same green box in both
noise enters the add node from below as a labelled side input; the step index k and the previous state enter the network from the top and left
noised input, network, predicted noise, subtract and refined output on one horizontal line inside the panel

channels.colour: blue = previous state (conditioning), orange = the prediction being refined, green = predicted noise; light-green fill also marks the network box, so green carries two meanings
channels.shape: tall rounded box = network, waveform = state or noise, circled plus/minus = arithmetic
channels.line: solid = data within a step, dashed = hand-off between the initial prediction and the refinement and the loop between steps
channels.frame: grey rounded panel = one refinement step

quality.strengths: The loop is the method and is drawn as one: a framed step with a single labelled dashed return; every intermediate the step compares is drawn as data (the noised input, the predicted noise, the refined output) rather than a wire into a block; the network is the same shape and fill in both stages; noise and k are short labels at the node that uses them.
quality.weaknesses: The dashed loop travels around the bottom of the whole panel instead of a short return; the curved line from the noised input to the subtract node bends under the network; green is both the network fill and the predicted-noise colour; the decreasing noise level across steps, which the caption calls the point, is only a subscript in the noise label.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
